senses.sense: A ground truth of Physick on which the physician must build: that great and little world answer to each other, so that malady and medicine share one Physiognomy, Chyromancy and Anotomy; the text also calls it a Foundation.

evidence.quote: every malady and medicine is of the same Physiognomy, Chyromancy and Anotomy; He that knows not this Fundamentall cannot be a good Phisitian
this true Fundamentall of the occult Phylosophycal Physick
this firme and unmovable Foundation

senses.sense: A foundation of truth that is at once theological and philosophical, laid in faith and Regeneration, from which all sciences and true knowledge of Nature are attained.

evidence.quote: that invincible united Fundamentall of Theologicall and Phylosophicall Truth and perfect Piety
according to the Fundamentall knowledge of the same by the supernall help of the Light of Grace
All Sciences are perfectly attained unto by the Fundamentall of Faith and new Regeneration or Celestiall Transplantation

senses.sense: The invisible and insensible body of the Astra's, also called Nature; the invisible Man and the spirit of man's body are one and the same with it.

evidence.quote: That invisible and insensible body of the Astra's is the Spirit of the World, or Nature
is altogether one and the same thing with the Spirit of the world, as whitenesse is with snow
the spirit of the world (one and the same with the spirit of our body)
The Celestiall or that Spirit of the world and the Naturall Spirit of our body is one and the same Spirit

senses.sense: The matter of the chief Medicine, holding the force of all heavenly and earthly things, by which bodies and impure metals alike are restored; elsewhere the matter is pointed to without being named.

evidence.quote: that is, the Soule or Spirit of the world, which hath in it the force of all Celestiall and Terrestriall things
Imperfect and impure mettalls are cleansed from their infirmities and accidents by the same spirit of the world
even the most simple matter which the most Great God generated of the spirit of the world

senses.sense: The inner Heaven of Man, the invisible or sydereall man and body, which holds all the Astra's, comes from the Astra's of the Firmament and is the same with the Firmament; the author says neglect of it bred errors in Philosophy and Physick.

evidence.quote: the internall Heaven of Man, which is the Olimpick spirit, doth particularly comprehend all the Astra's
The invisible man or Olimpick Spirit is borne in us after this manner.
If Aristotle had taken notice of this Olympick Spirit, and Galen made more account of it, there had not such errors crept into Philosophy and Physick
the Sydereall, Internall, Olimpick. Incorporeall, or (Gabalis Homo) coagulated or curdled Man is the same with the Firmament of the Astra's

senses.sense: The Being of the seed: the inner Astrum, the Sun of the Microcosm, from which Man is generated, formed and governed; the name is given as Paracelsus's.

evidence.quote: which Paracelsus calls the Ens or Being of the seed and virtue or power

senses.sense: Agrippa's name for the universall Spirit that fills the world: a Being that the senses cannot grasp.

evidence.quote: Agrippa calleth it the subject of all mirability, the Ens or Being that cannot be comprehended by sence

senses.sense: The first Being toward life in nourishment: what rises from the last matter of the meat by the Archaeus, from which the body is fed.

evidence.quote: The first Ens or Being toward life, from whence the body hath it's nourishment & food ariseth out of the last matter of the Meat by the Archaeus

senses.sense: The Ens of God: the divine source of certain diseases, whose causes cannot be searched out and whose cure is sought in Faith, not in Nature.

evidence.quote: Paracelsus calleth them Deal diseases, which are from the Ens of God, who inflicteth all such diseases
The Causes of those diseases that are of the Ens of God are unsearchable, here the cure must be sought in Faith, not in Nature

senses.sense: The Being as one of the two ways life is shortened: the source of bodily (Entall or Corporall) diseases, whose cure is sought from natural causes and means; a Latin margin note names MENS and ENS together beside the two ways.

evidence.quote: The life is shortned PER ENTEM
by the Being, as by Entall or Corporall diseases
And this cure of the harmes of the Naturall members which come from the Ens or Being, is to be sought from Natural causes and means
MENS & ENS abrumpunt nobis vitam.

senses.sense: The source of one of two kinds of death, a death the physician cannot hinder, set against death from the Iliad. Several defensible readings: (a) the Ens of God of CH5.82, whose cure lies in Faith, not Nature; (b) the bodily Being of CH6.74, which bears the same words 'Ens or Being', though there its harms are to be cured by natural means. The lines given do not settle which.

evidence.quote: the death which is from the resolution of the Iliad may be hindred by the industry of the Physitian, but that which is from the Ens or Being cannot
There is a two fold death, from the Iliad or first principle, and from the Ens or Being.
here the cure must be sought in Faith, not in Nature
which come from the Ens or Being, is to be sought from Natural causes and means

senses.sense: The inner Astrum or syderiall spirit in each thing, from which its formation, figure, colour and smell proceed from within, not from the stars without; a margin note likens the forming in the Astra's to iron in the imagination of the Smith.

evidence.quote: a syderiall spirit, which is called Heaven or the Astrum, the secret Forger, from which every Formation, Figure and Colour of things proceedeth
all things proceed from the inner Astrum or secret forger, and not from without
as iron in the imagination of the Smith

senses.sense: The image in a maker's mind of what he will form, used as a likeness for how things are formed in the Astra's.

evidence.quote: as iron in the imagination of the Smith

senses.sense: A name of the sydereall body of man: it holds and is all the Astra's, keeps their course, nature and power, and is one with the Astra's of the Firmament; therefore it works many operations.

evidence.quote: It is also called ahe imagination, which incloseth all the Astra's, and is indeed all the Astra's or Starrs and holdeth the same course, Nature and power with heaven
whereas the imagination of Man is not one, but all the Astra's, it is as true that it produceth not onely one, but many operations
the whole Imagination of Man dependeth on the Astra's of the Firmament, yea is the same and abideth one with them

senses.sense: A forming and working power of man, the ground of Gabalisticall Magick: it marks the unborn child, draws other men's fantasie like the Loadstone, infects the stars, breeds the Plague, and can produce growing things and metals.

evidence.quote: The child in the mothers womb is strangely marked by the impression of the imagination without any bodily touch
Thus the Imagination breedeth the Plague and such like Firmamentall diseases; it brings sicknesse and health.
Thus by Imagination and true Gabalia all hearbs, all growing things, all mettalls may be produced.
Thirdly, by a strongly exalted IMAGINATION
The Imagination or Fantasie of Man is like the Load stone in its Nature, attracting the Fantasie of other men
but Man rather inclines the Stars, and by his Magicall imagination infecteth them

senses.sense: Naturall Faith, inborn from the first Creation, as distinct from the Faith of Grace: it can both cause and cure diseases.

evidence.quote: Naturall Faith (I speak not of the Faith of Grace by Christ) inborn of God the Father in the first Creation, which is our IMAGINATION, is so powerfull that it can both cause and cure diseases
when out of his own proper Imagination, from fear and terrour it breedeth that Basilisk of Heaven

senses.sense: An imagining power that the Firmament, and the whole Heaven, also has, but without Reason, as man has it with Reason.

evidence.quote: it must needs be that the Firmament also hath an Imagination but without Reason, as Man the off-spring of the world hath with Reason
The whole Heaven is nothing else but the Imagination

senses.sense: The imagination of the five Spirits in the Elements, which must also be in man and is bound by his Reason used according to God's will.

evidence.quote: the Imagination also of these five Spirits in the Elements must be in the Microcosm Man
but the use of Mans Reason according to the will and command of God, is as a Chaine

senses.sense: One of five invisible mental harms that come by the Mind and shorten life, cured by Faith or magical means, not by bodily medicine.

evidence.quote: whence arise mentall diseases which are invisible, and affect us in our Mind, as Inchantment, Imagination, Estimation, Influence; Superstition
i. e. Inchantment, Imagination, Estimation, Influence, Superstition.

senses.sense: The sign in Heaven that each living creature has; Ascendants are among the things over which Magick or Faith has power.

evidence.quote: every living Creature hath its Ascendant signe in Heaven
Magick or Faith transplanting minds hath power over all Spirits and Ascendants.

senses.sense: The Ascendant as a supposed source of man's conditions and manners, denied: these come from God through the breath of life.

evidence.quote: For we receive not our conditions, properties, and manners from the Ascendant, nor from the Constellation of the Planets, but from the hand of God through the breathing in of the breath of life

senses.sense: The seed of a plant, from which it grows and in which another of its kind lies hid.

evidence.quote: As a Tree groweth from the seed, the seed is the beginning of the Tree, and the seed also is the end of the Tree

senses.sense: The Astrum, the invisible body in a thing, which brings forth a visible body; the Earth and its fruits hold such seeds.

evidence.quote: the seeds of any graine or Wheat is the Astrum, viz. the invisible body, which being cast into the Earth it produceth a visible body
every one of these fruits is againe the Astrum and Seed
Though the Earth seem to be dead, yet hath it in it selfe the seeds and seminall vertues of all things
the fruits of those Astra's or Caelestiall, Ayry, Earthy, Watry seeds doe indeavour and bend to one generall Good

senses.sense: In the passage given out of Severinus: the hidden seminal causes planted in the Elements at the Creation, joined with the Astra's, which bring forth what is treasured in them, open the use of the Elements, and imitate the order of the world.

evidence.quote: to the Seeds that they may produce out of themselves the things that were secretly treasured up in them
The Seeds and Astra's, those bonds of things, lay hid in the invisible Treasures of the Elements from the beginning of the Creation
The knowledge of the Elements cannot be attained unto without these Seeds, because they declare or open the use and services of the Elements
all the least and smallest Seeds strive to imitate the oeconomy of the world, and hold forth a dark resemblance of the Elements and Principles

senses.sense: The first, pure seeds of things, which spring up in the four Elements as wombs and in which the roots of sickness were mixed after the Fall.

evidence.quote: implanted and mixt in the pure and first seeds of things
the nourishments of Naturall things are the fruits of those seeds which spring up in the foure wombs or Elements

senses.sense: The origin from which a whole world comes: the first matter is the seed of all created things, the great world the seed of Man, and the Word FIAT the seed of the whole world.

evidence.quote: so the great world is the seed of Adam or Man
So the First Matter (which Paracelsus calleth the Limbus, whose Earth was the WORD of the Lord) was the seed of all things that were to be created
which is the generall seed of all things or subject of the first matter
by this Word, FIAT, the seed of the whole world, were Heaven and Earth created

senses.sense: Man as the last and perfect seed of the world, able to beget another man; the text itself says Man is not a seed as other seed is.

evidence.quote: and Man was the last of all as the perfect seed, which againe is able out of himselfe to beget another Man like himself
And though Man be not a seed as other seed is, yet hath he power to cast seed out of himselfe

senses.sense: The seeds of all things, which lie hid in Man, as in a field that holds all seeds.

evidence.quote: yea and that the seeds of all things lye hid in him
that Earth or field which hath all seeds in it self

senses.sense: Interpreted: the truth planted from God, by Regeneration, in which true Philosophy grows; among the Gentiles that seed was choked for want of the Sun. The likeness is marked by 'like', and the same paragraph says the Truth is planted in Christians who have their seed from God.

evidence.quote: that seed which among the Gentiles was choaked for want of the Sun, like that among the thorns
Christians onely in whom the Truth is planted, who have their seed from God, by the means of Regeneration which the Heathen have not

senses.sense: The four Elements, Fire, Aire, Water and Earth: man's matter is their extract, God made them to feed and heal man, and knowing them shows every disease and its cure.

evidence.quote: And because the Matter of Man is the Extract of the four Elements, it is requisite that he have in himselfe a familiarity with all the Elements and their fruits
God created the Elements for their fruits sake, that they might sustaine and preserve Man with food and Physick.
The knowledge of the 4 Elements doe shew every disease in man and its cure.

senses.sense: The four bodies into which the three Principles of the first matter were afterwards separated.

evidence.quote: afterward these three Species are seperated into four divers bodies, or Elements

senses.sense: In the passage given out of Severinus: the true Elements, which are spiritual, the places, wombs and receptacles of the whole Creation and its life and act.

evidence.quote: The true and purely spirituall Elements are the keepers, nurses, places, Mines, wombs and receptacles of the whole Creation
for the true Elements are Spirituall

senses.sense: In the passage given out of Severinus: the Elementated Elements, the four as they are to us, which conceive, bring forth and take back all things.

evidence.quote: There are to us four Elementated Elements, viz. Fire or the Firmament, Aire, Water, Earth, which conceive, bring forth, and againe receive or take into them all things

senses.sense: The Element as the invisible life and spirit within its visible body, in which the Astra's lie; the visible Earth is not the Element but its body.

evidence.quote: The Externall is not the Element, but the body of the Element, and is the Sulphur, Mercury, Salt; For the Element of the Earth is life and Spirit wherein lie the Astra's of the Earth
The Earth of it self is dead, yet is it the Element of an invisible and hidden life.

senses.sense: One of the three Principles of every natural body, beside Mercury and Sulphur: it gives solidity, colour and taste, remains in the ashes when wood burns, and is separated from simples and from food.

evidence.quote: Into Mercury or liquor, Sulphur or Oyle, and Salt
The Salt by coagulation gives Solidity, Colour and Tast to all bodies
The third, viz. the Salt is unctuous, very little, thin and lasting, and remains in the ashes.
a bitter hot Salt penetrating by a subtile resolution and causing sweat
the superfluity of Salt is separated by the Urine

senses.sense: A wider use the author explains in another writer's words: whatever melts, resolves into a watery moisture and is then dried and hardened by fire; the margin beside it calls all earthiness the Salt of Paracelsus.

evidence.quote: sometime he calls that Salt whatever it be that will melt, and may be resolved into a watry moysture, and then dryed and hardened by Fire
All Terresterity is the Salt of Paracelsus.

senses.sense: Salt named together with Mummy as one thing, whose spending leaves things to breed worms.

evidence.quote: When the Salt or Mummy is spent

senses.sense: One of the three Principles of every natural body, the oily one: it tempers the Salt's coagulation and gives substance and Transmutation; it is separated from simples such as Opium and from food.

evidence.quote: Into Mercury or liquor, Sulphur or Oyle, and Salt
The Sulphur by a pleasant mixture tempereth the coagulation of the Salt, and gives the Body Substance and Transmutation
the body of the Element, and is the Sulphur, Mercury, Salt
in Opium there is a sweet Narcotick Sulphur
that of Sulphure is divided and purged through the Entrals

senses.sense: Interpreted: the vitall Sulphur, a life-bearing Sulphur in bodies, which holds the true Medicine as the treasure of Nature and which the Plague infects in man; named beside Mummy in both places. The lines do not say more of what it is.

evidence.quote: this Medicine, as naturall Mummy and kernell of Nature, is contained in the vitall Sulphur, as in the treasure of Nature
it infecteth the Mummy and Sulphur of the microcosm, Man

senses.sense: The matter God first produced by the word FIAT, threefold in the three Principles, a confused Essence called the Chaos and Hylen and by Paracelsus the Limbus, out of which every creature was drawn; it was made a world.

evidence.quote: By the word FIAT (or Let there be) God produced the first matter, which is threefold in respect of the three Principles contained in the first
which was a kind of ineffigiate confused Essence, which Phylosophers call the Chaos and Hylen, or Mother of the world
So the First Matter (which Paracelsus calleth the Limbus, whose Earth was the WORD of the Lord) was the seed of all things that were to be created
The first matter was made a world, and the great World was made Man.
so God extracted every creature out of the first matter.
ALL things in respect of the first matter were created perfect

senses.sense: The creating word of God, 'Let there be', by which the first matter, all things threefold, and man out of the dust of the Earth were made.

evidence.quote: By the word FIAT (or Let there be) God produced the first matter
For the Holy Triunity when it spake that Triune word FIAT created all things Triune
Man was created è Limo Terrae, out of the clay or dust of the Earth, by the word FIAT

senses.sense: The Word FIAT as what works in all creatures and heals: the seed of the whole world, by which God's Spirit is one with Nature, called the true medicine.

evidence.quote: This Word then is the true medicine that healeth all things
by this Word, FIAT, the seed of the whole world, were Heaven and Earth created, and this is that which is efficacious in all the Creatures
by the Spirit of God made One with Nature by his Word FIAT

senses.sense: The source of the second of man's two Spirits, set against the first, which is from the Limbus.

evidence.quote: The first Spirit is from the Limbus or greater world; the second from the word Fiat.

senses.sense: A fourth Principle that some Theophrastaeans add to Salt, Sulphur and Mercury: it can be got from Mineralls and Vegetables but not from Animalls, and answers to Aire.

evidence.quote: which they call the Spirit, which though it may be got out of Mineralls and Vegetables
Mercury to Water, Spirit to Aire

senses.sense: The syderiall spirit in all things, the Astrum: an invisible, insensible, living body, without Reason in growing things and with Reason in man.

evidence.quote: are indued with a syderiall spirit, which is called Heaven or the Astrum
But the Astrum is nothing else but the insensible, invisible body, or living Spirit, yet without Reason in things that grow; but with reason in living things

senses.sense: Man's two Spirits: one syderiall, from the Firmament; the other from the breath of life, the Intellectuall Soul inspired from God.

evidence.quote: There are two Spirits in Man
one a syderiall Spirit from the Firmament, the other from the breath of life, which is the Intellectuall Soul inspired from God

senses.sense: The Spirit of God moving upon the face of the Waters at the Creation; the margin sets it beside the fourth Principle called the Spirit, without saying how the two belong together.

evidence.quote: and of the Spirit moving upon the face of the Waters
The Spirit of God upon the face of the waters.

senses.sense: The universall Spirit that lives in and quickens the whole mass of the world and fills it.

evidence.quote: That universall Spirit which liveth in and quickneth this whole Masse, which worketh all in all, and filleth the whole world

senses.sense: The spirit got out of things by art, also called the supernall Fire: the life and Balsom of all natural things.

evidence.quote: the spirit or that supernall Fire is got out of them by art
The Spirit is the life and Balsom of all Naturall things.

senses.sense: Interpreted: the four Elementary Spirits, spirits belonging to the four Elements, called the inhabitants of the world; with a fifth kind they are five, whose Imagination is in man.

evidence.quote: the four Elementary Spirits of the four inhabitants of the world
the Imagination also of these five Spirits in the Elements must be in the Microcosm Man

senses.sense: True and lawful Magick, set apart from witchcraft: the perfection of philosophy and full knowledge of hidden Nature, which works wonders beyond Nature's usual order by applying Agents and Patients according to the consent and dissent of things; far better treasures lie in it.

evidence.quote: every were I mean that which is True and lawfull
or wichcraft, which is fit for none but Vulcan, and deserveth to be burned
the absolute perfection of the whole most noble Phylosophy, the chiefest Wisdome of Gods works and the plenary knowledge of occult Nature
doth things exceeding the usuall order of Nature, by a fit application of Agents and Patients, observing the consent and dissent of things
in the true Cabala, Magick and Woarchadumie, there are laid up far better Treasures

senses.sense: Naturall Magick and its kinds: Gamahaea, which does by Art invisibly what Nature does visibly, and the Gabalisticall part, which works through the Imagination; the margin sets Magick beside Faith transplanting minds.

evidence.quote: This fourth kind of Naturall Magick called Gamahaea doth all things invisibly and spiritually, by the help of Art, which Nature is able to doe visibly and corporally without such help.
This part of Magick is called Gabalisticall, and is supported with three Pillars.
Hence the true Magician or wise Man can attract the operation of the Astra's, stones, mettalls, &c. into the Imagination
Magick or Faith transplanting minds hath power over all Spirits and Ascendants.
thus by reall Magick he shewed to that great Picus the hidden virtue or power of Man

senses.sense: Interpreted: God's hidden, ongoing working by which what was planted in the Elements at the Creation is always supplied out of Divine Wisdom; the passage says only that this Magick is incomprehensible.

evidence.quote: shall ever be supplyed by an incomprehensible Magick out of the Eternall Treasures of Divine Wisdome

senses.sense: Mechanick Magick: an art by whose help the Element of Earth should swim upon water; the lines given say no more of it.

evidence.quote: that the Element of EARTH should by the help of Mechanick Magick swim upon the water
